A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same output dimension collapse diagnostic and sparse-translator analysis. Their main text, figures, equations and complete Appendices A and B support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original Deeprecon reconstruction and prediction-error analyses, finite-sample simulations, and repeated-stimulus noise estimation.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds category-overlap, additional-subject, generator-prior and CLIP-feature analyses.

M1.justification: The best-prediction projection and correlation-based variable selection followed by ridge regression are retained. Algorithm 1 documents the existing projection computation; the DGN and CLIP additions are evaluation variants.

E1.justification: V3 adds a natural-image category-overlap scenario alongside the existing held-out-category and artificial-shape tests (Fig. A1). Deeprecon coverage and the four synthetic generative conditions otherwise remain.

E2.justification: The naive and sparse regression comparators, Shen et al. (2019) reconstruction reference, and Ozcelik–VanRullen (2023) pipeline are retained. The latter comparison moves from v2 Fig. A2 to v3 Fig. A6. New controls reuse the existing translator comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 substantially expands the evaluation design: it constructs category overlap by replacing 50 training categories, evaluates sub-02 and sub-03, tests a DGN prior, and adds a CLIP-target comparison using a naive ridge penalty of 60,000 (Appendices B.4 and B.10). These are additional protocols; the original experiments' principal settings are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds checks of category mismatch (Fig. A1), subject dependence (A3–A4), generator-prior dependence (A5), and feature-representation dependence (A7), plus a noise–sparsity sensitivity map (Fig. 9C). These substantially broaden the robustness questions beyond v2's retained training-size and simulation analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across samples and the same repeated-stimulus noise-variance analysis. Additional subjects use the existing reporting practice. No new seed counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The main reported approximately 70% natural-image and 40% artificial-image error proportions are retained. V3 adds results showing persistent collapse under category overlap, additional subjects and a DGN prior. It also reports nearly equal CLIP-target errors with no sparse advantage (Fig. A7), and new noise–sparsity trends (Fig. 9C). These are substantial additions under new conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds an explicit centering decomposition and almost-sure convergence argument to the correlation/inner-product approximation. Appendix B.3 adds centered-Gram rank and computational-cost properties. The principal error and hit-rate formulas remain unchanged; their presentation as Corollary 1 and Theorem 1 mainly reorganizes existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list recast the ODC contribution as practical diagnosis and formalization based on a standard regression property, rather than foregrounding a theoretical demonstration of collapse. The diagnostic becomes more prominent, while the conditional sparsity-benefit claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 already qualifies sparsity benefits by noise and representation structure. V3 explains distributed CLIP and fully connected features as potentially mismatched to local sparsity, connects the added CLIP result to this boundary, and explicitly states that sparsity does not always improve performance. Existing nonlinear-translator and latent-versus-image-error limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds projection pseudocode, Gram-matrix reuse and multiplication-order guidance, explicitly identifies VGG19 features and test-fMRI averaging for retained analyses, and documents the new controls and CLIP penalty. Both PDFs already link to the same code repository.

R1.justification: V3 adds Dosovitskiy and Brox (2016) for the DGN prior and clarifies positioning around the standard regression property underlying ODC. The new Related work section largely relocates existing background. Onoo et al.'s publication update refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V3 revises the abstract, introduction and selected explanations, collects existing background into Related work, organizes the theory into named statements, and adds a Broader Impact Statement. These are localized reorganizations; the main argument and analysis sequence remain.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the visual evidence with new Figs. A1, A3–A5 and A7, and adds the sensitivity panel to Fig. 9. It also revises Fig. 3's axis presentation and relocates retained supplementary figures: v2 A1 and A2 become v3 A2 and A6.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the existing evidence with category-overlap, additional-subject and generator-prior controls. The CLIP result and sensitivity map make applicability limits more concrete, while Algorithm 1 and clearer novelty framing improve usability and interpretation. These are targeted improvements to the principal derivations, simulations and real-data findings already present in v2.
